domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave. Owned by the requesting employee; acted upon by their manager. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through final resolution.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Acts as the template from which employee balances are derived. Enforces constraints like minimum notice, accrual caps, and whether manager approval is required.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Owns leave requests and leave balances. The managerId establishes the approval hierarchy for leave requests.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining days for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted when a leave request is approved; restored if an approved request is cancelled/revoked.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Categorizes the kind of leave being requested. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that governs its rules. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumerates the lifecycle states of a LeaveRequest. Drives state-transition validation and determines which actions are permissible at each stage.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation in the leave management domain. Required by GP-002. Captures what changed, who changed it, and when. Actions include CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT.

modules.name: leave-type
owns: LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity)

modules.name: leave-status
owns: LeaveStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — shared, leave-type, leave-status
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules. shared provides BaseEntity, BaseRepository, error types, and DB connection. leave-type and leave-status are pure enums with no dependencies. These must exist before anything else can be built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Supporting services — employee, audit, policy
recommended_phases.rationale: employee depends only on shared. audit depends only on shared. policy depends on shared + leave-type. These three are independent of each other and can be built in parallel. They provide the supporting services that leave orchestration will consume.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Balance and notification
recommended_phases.rationale: balance depends on shared + leave-type + employee. notification depends on shared + employee. Both need employee from Phase 2. They are independent of each other and can be built in parallel.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Leave orchestration — service, controller, routes, validation
recommended_phases.rationale: The leave module is the aggregate root and orchestrator. It depends on every module from Phases 1–3. It wires together policy validation, balance deduction, audit recording, and notification dispatch into the submit/approve/reject/cancel workflows.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Feature Architecture

### Overview

The leave management module enables employees to apply for annual, sick, and emergency leave, managers to approve or reject requests, and the system to track leave balances. It is implemented as a modular monolith using TypeScript, Fastify, React Native, and PostgreSQL, following the existing architectural principles defined in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`.

### Domain Entities

- **LeaveRequest** — aggregate root; lifecycle: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED.
- **LeavePolicy** — defines rules per leave type; lifecycle: ACTIVE, INACTIVE.
- **Employee** — owns requests and balances; lifecycle: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED.
- **LeaveBalance** — tracks entitlement per employee per policy per fiscal year; lifecycle: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN, CLOSED.
- **LeaveType** — enum: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity.
- **LeaveStatus** — enum: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED.
- **AuditLog** — immutable record of all state changes (GP-002).

### Module Boundaries

| Module | Path | Responsibility |
|--------|------|----------------|
| `shared` | `src/shared/` | BaseEntity, BaseRepository, error types, DB connection |
| `leave-type` | `src/modules/leave-type/` | LeaveType enum |
| `leave-status` | `src/modules/leave-status/` | LeaveStatus enum |
| `employee` | `src/modules/employee/` | Employee model, service, repository, controller, routes |
| `audit` | `src/modules/audit/` | AuditLog model, service, repository |
| `policy` | `src/modules/policy/` | LeavePolicy model, service, repository |
| `balance` | `src/modules/balance/` | LeaveBalance model, service, repository |
| `notification` | `src/modules/notification/` | Notification model, service |
| `leave` | `src/modules/leave/` | LeaveRequest aggregate, service, repository, controller, routes, validation |

### Conceptual Data Model

Six tables (no DDL — migrations generated from this spec):

- **employees** — core employee data with self-referencing manager hierarchy.
- **leave_types** — lookup table for leave type codes.
- **leave_policies** — per-type entitlement rules, linked to leave_types.
- **leave_requests** — the core leave application entity with status lifecycle.
- **leave_balances** — per-employee, per-type, per-fiscal-year tracking.
- **audit_logs** — immutable audit trail for all state-changing operations.

All tables use UUID primary keys and standard timestamp columns (`created_at`, `updated_at`). Foreign keys enforce referential integrity. Indexes are defined for common query patterns: employee lookups, status filtering, date-range overlap detection, and audit retrieval.

### Service Interfaces

- **ILeaveService** — submit, approve, reject, cancel, get requests.
- **IBalanceService** — get/deduct/credit/initialize balances.
- **IPolicyService** — get policies, validate requests.
- **IAuditService** — record and retrieve audit entries.
- **IEmployeeService** — get employee, manager, direct reports, authorization checks.
- **INotificationService** — notify employees and managers of status changes.

### Dependency Map

```
leave → shared, leave-type, leave-status, employee, policy, balance, audit, notification
balance → shared, leave-type, employee
policy → shared, leave-type
employee → shared
audit → shared
notification → shared, employee
```

### Implementation Phases

1. **Foundation** — shared, leave-type, leave-status (zero-dependency leaf modules).
2. **Supporting Services** — employee, audit, policy (can be built in parallel).
3. **Balance & Notification** — balance and notification (depend on employee from Phase 2).
4. **Leave Orchestration** — leave module as aggregate root, wiring all services together.

### Key Business Rules Enforced

- State transitions are strictly validated (BR-001).
- Balance sufficiency checked before approval (BR-002).
- Balance deducted on approval, restored on revocation (BR-003, BR-004).
- Only the designated manager can approve/reject (BR-005).
- Only active employees can submit requests (BR-006).
- Only active policies can be used (BR-007).
- No overlapping approved leave (BR-008).
- Date range validity and minimum notice period enforced (BR-009, BR-010).

### Compliance with Golden Principles

- **GP-002 (Audit)**: Every state change on leave_requests and leave_balances is recorded in audit_logs via IAuditService.
- **GP-003 (Input Validation)**: All inputs validated at the controller boundary using leave.validation.ts.
- **GP-005 (RBAC)**: Controller methods enforce that the authenticated user is the employee (for submit/cancel) or the manager (for approve/reject) via IEmployeeService.isManagerOf().

This architecture replaces the previous flat-file module sketches and consolidates the domain, data, and application designs into a single coherent specification.
sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — list direct reports for manager approval workflows; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated employees for leave eligibility checks

table leave_types | fields: id, code, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code (annual, sick, emergency, etc.); is_active: filter active leave types for request forms and policy assignment

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_id, policy_name, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join to leave type for policy lookups; is_active: filter active policies during leave request validation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for an employee (self-service dashboard); status: filter by status for approval queues (SUBMITTED) and reporting; leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: list requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for a specific employee (self-service dashboard); employee_id, leave_type_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup — one balance row per employee per leave type per fiscal year; leave_type_id: aggregate balance queries by leave type; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year for accrual and reset jobs

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: audit records by actor; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports
